title: A long neck in pieces
hook: A neck contains a chain of bones.

knows: Vertebrae are bones arranged along the spine.
doesNotKnow: Connect vertebral evidence to constrained models rather than a certain pose.

misconception: A fossil neck proves one exact living posture.
objective: Connect vertebral evidence to constrained models rather than a certain pose.

claims.text: A neck contains a chain of bones. An articulated sauropod neck preserves vertebrae and their joints. What can that evidence help scientists investigate? The schematic neck shows a series of linked vertebrae. Their forms and joints can inform models of support and possible movement, but a fossil skeleton alone does not fix an exact pose during life.

claims.text: The figure is a simplified, not-to-scale schematic of a stated example, not an image of an identified specimen.
Recall: A fossil neck preserves joints between vertebrae. What might their shapes help constrain? Joint shapes can inform possible movement without recording every posture.
